output.reasoning: The posting fails three of the labeling criteria. (1) Role type: 'Applied AI Architect, Partnerships' is a pre-sales, partner-facing solutions architecture role. The work is cultivating relationships with GSIs/RSIs and cloud partners, evangelizing, supporting deals, running events and workshops, and gathering product feedback. It is not hands-on building, training, or deploying of ML/NLP systems, so it does not match her target roles (Machine Learning Engineer, AI Engineer, Applied NLP Engineer, ML Engineer, Research Engineer), even though the department is 'Applied AI'. (2) Level: it explicitly asks for '5+ years of experience in technical customer-facing/partner-facing roles such as Solutions Architect, Sales Engineer...' plus a track record with GSIs and cloud providers. That is well beyond a new grad finishing an MS in CS at Boston University (ending 2026-12) with one 8-month ML Engineer co-op. (3) Location: the role is in Munich, Germany, under a hybrid policy requiring at least 25% office time. It is neither US-based nor designated Remote. Her willingness to relocate covers only the US. Skills: the required section names only AWS and GCP as specific technologies. Since fewer than 2 of those are in her shipped list (AWS yes, GCP no), this would also fail the skills test, though that test is not needed to reject the posting. Sponsorship: Anthropic states 'We do sponsor visas!' with caveats and does not explicitly disclaim it, so sponsorship is not a blocker. Even so, the role-type, experience-level, and location mismatches each make this NOT_RELEVANT on their own.
